title: Edward I essay success criteria
subject: History
unit: Spring 2: Medieval monarchs: Magna Carta and Edward I
source: Written for history/y7 lesson 13 (Edward I essay success criteria (portal printable; assessed))
intro: Lesson 13: Edward's wars in Wales and Scotland. Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: Wales
points: Llywelyn ap Gruffudd, Prince of Wales

model.title: Conclusion: how successful was Edward I?

parts.text: Weigh: laws and Parliament were lasting successes
Weigh: Wales conquered, Scotland lost, huge debts
Weigh: the 1290 expulsion of the Jews was a grave injustice
Judge: successful in power, not in justice to all

keywords.def: taking control of a land by force
a ruler who claims power over other rulers

questions.q: Explain why Edward was more successful in Wales than Scotland. (4 marks)
questions.a: Wales: Llywelyn killed, castles built, statute imposed (2). Scotland: larger, strong resistance from Wallace and Bruce, Edward died before finishing (2)

questions.q: Core (assessed): In the portal response box, write paragraphs 4 and 5 (Wales; Scotland) and your conclusion: 'How successful was Edward I?'
questions.a: End-of-unit essay assessed: knowledge, explanation, judgement against criteria

questions.q: Extend: Add one interpretation and say whether you agree.
questions.a: Engages with an interpretation using evidence

questions.q: Who won the Battle of Stirling Bridge (1297)?
questions.a: B) William Wallace. Wallace and Andrew Moray defeated the English army.

questions.q: Big question: can a conqueror be successful if never accepted?
questions.a: Militarily perhaps, but lasting success needs acceptance; Scotland shows force alone failed
